title: "Integrating MWEB in Cake Wallet"
description: Digital privacy, security, and freedom advocate Tuxsudo goes over Integrating MWEB in Cake Wallet.

asr.full_text: Digital privacy security and freedom advocate. Please welcome Tux Sudoh from Cake. Okay, hey guys! Hope you all doing well. We're glad to sponsor Litecoin 2025. We came here last year and we first introduced M-Web and our integration into the app with you all. And it's been almost a year since we did that in Nashville and there's been a lot of improvements since then. And we hope you all will take a look, if you haven't already, at M-Web inside Cake Wallet. So this'll be partially rehashing some of the privacy features that come with using Mweb and also somewhat of an update report on the features we have improved in our app. So first off, what exactly is MimbleWimble? So MimbleWimble is basically a privacy protocol that enables several privacy features that improves fungibility inherently due to those privacy features as well as improving scalability. It also happens to be the tongue-tying curse from Harry Potter, which is kind of a funny name there. The protocol is tongue-tied – it can't speak to the details of the transaction. How is MenbleWimble integrated into litecoin so mimblewimble is integrated into litecoin with what's called mmweb which stands for the mimblewimble extension block the mimblewimble extension block essentially combines the privacy protocol mimblewimble and allows it to work within litecoin as a almost like a side chain right it's an extension block it runs on the same block time as the transparent litecoin network and allows you to go in and out of it. So, uh Mweb has a few specific privacy features that make it really good. And each of these features on their own isn't inherently that powerful, but when you combine them together you kind of compound your privacy gains and all three of those, these things together along with a few other things I haven't mentioned, all these privacy improvements together makes for quite a great and powerful privacy upgrade to what is traditionally a transparent blockchain. And a few of these things which I will get into a little more detail of the main ones I would say are confidential transactions stealth addresses as well as they coin join and so to boil these down a little bit and once again there's lots of other things going on behind-the-scenes with MWeb these are the three main ones that provide the bulk of the privacy the confidential transactions those essentially hides the amount that you're sending to someone typically within litecoin because it's fully transparent if I were to send you zero point one LTC I want to send you around ten dollars u.s. I send you 0.1 LTC that number is visible on the blockchain if somebody looks up your address or my address they can see that there was a transaction from this address to another address that was zero point 1 LTC. Confidential transactions uses zero knowledge proofs to hide the amount and more specifically, they're using range proofs to make sure there's no funny business going on. To make sure that the amount is within a specific range, so an individual can't just create Litecoin out of thin air and the coin join attempts to hide the real sender by essentially just mixing inputs from multiple transactions. And this is an improvement. It could be improved later on. There's been some talks about improving this, because CoinJoin inherently isn't the best way to do sender privacy, but it is a great improvement over nothing for sure. And then the last main one is stealth addresses this is a really cool but simple way to prevent the issues of address reuse so when you have mWeb turned on you have this new address type that starts with mWeb and this address type has a public key in it so if I were to send 0.1 LTC to your mWeb address by wallet all behind the scenes is going to take a public key from that address and it's going to generate a unique one-time key that shows up on chain that only you can know is yours and only you can spend from. So every time somebody sends you Litecoin to your M Web address it's not inherently tied to that specific M Web address like it normally we would be with Transparent Litecoin. So this is really powerful for especially donations or if you want to address on a website. But you don't want people being able to look up that address and see exactly how much is currently in it, how much you've gotten and where the money's gone after that. So all these privacy improvements are great but they're not without some potential downsides and some cons which I think for mWeb are actually pretty minor. So the main one is that it does require a bit of work on the device. It requires some on device scanning, now for mWeb specifically it's actually pretty lightweight, it's actually really fast. It does require downloading around 600 megabytes of data which is the Litecoin block headers, so can scan through those blocks and see if any and when inputs belong to you however it is very quick so the main downside is probably just the initial data requirement but this is initial once you do the initial scan of the block headers you only have to do the next blocks going forward right so if you haven't opened you all in the week you might have a few thousand blocks to scan through, but if you open it once a day, you only have not that many, a few hundred. And the other down side is that coinjoin is a weaker way to do sender privacy. Once again, it is better than nothing, but it's definitely not the best, and there has definitely been talks about improving in the future, maybe getting closer to something like Monera with ring signatures, or maybe even further beyond that so to actually enable nweb in cake wallet so our interface has definitely improved a lot since I last showed this off but the way to enable it's pretty much still the same once you create your litecoin wallet on cake wallet you'll be presented with this extra card underneath the initial Litecoin balanced card. And that's just explaining to you what M-web is. It's got a link to our documentation, which explains even further. If you tap Enable that, you will get that notice about it needing to download around 600 megabytes, might be a bit more than that now, of data, which is the block headers. And once it does that, it will go ahead and scan through the blocks. You can see on the top, it's gotta scan through all the blocks. And once that's done, you're able to use MWeb. And I'd say, depending on your internet connection, it only takes around 10 to 20 minutes to initially set that up. And that's the worst part of it. After you've done that, the bulk of it's done. And the actual onboarding process for MWeb is much easier than it has been before. We've got these new buttons that say Peg In and Peg Out. And basically what these mean is, if you're pegged in to MWeb, you're basically sending your transparent Litecoin into the MWeb extension block. And if you're pegged out then, you're basically taking MWeb out into the transparent Litecoin network. And this is much easier than it was before. Last year you had to copy your address, put it in the send screen, and put a specific amount and hop the it takes the transparent Litecoin and gives it to Mweb. It will filter by transparent Litecoin and you swipe to send and you can. It's going to filter it only by your Transparent Litecoin. And then you just swipe to Send, and you can see it's going to your M-Web address. And just like that, you've sent to some of your Transparent Litecoin into the M-Web network. I do want to reiterate that you don't have to initially do that just to send to an M-Web address. This is just recommended to enhance your privacy even further, going ahead and just sending some Transparent Litecoin initially into M-Web and leaving it there. And then a few other updates, we have easier onboarding like I just showed you guys. We also have the ability to use a custom Node with MWeb now. Before initially we had our own node hard coded into the app, but now you have the ability to use your own custom MWeb Node from the settings, and you can also rescan from a specific block height. So if there was maybe an input that you think it missed or something happened to your wallet, instead of having to create a whole new wallet and restore, you can just rescan from a specific block height. And another really great improvement. Unfortunately, this is only on Android. You'll have to scream at Apple for making this really impossible for us. We now have a background sync feature and this really helps to mitigate some of that scanning requirement that is happens because of MWeb because usually if you're just using litecoin transparently you open the wallet app and it's just connecting it's basically synchronized instantly but with MWeb you might have to wait just a little bit. Background sync helps mitigate that as an issue and background sync will allow cake wallet to wait just a little bit. Background sync helps mitigate that as an issue and background sync will allow CakeWallet to do just that, synchronize in the background. And so the idea is that when you go to open your wallet next either it'll be fully synced or it'll be almost all the way synced and you have just a few blocks just to do. And this is highly customizable. You can choose how aggressive the scheduling is for the sync. You can choose if it does it on battery, if it requires it to be charging You can change the data requirements and this works across pretty much all the other cryptos in the app, too, as well as Emweb for Litecoin. But once again, unfortunately it is Android-only, we're trying to figure out to see if we can maybe do some weird workarounds to get it to work on iOS, but that's just how Apple rolls. I want to quickly just go over the adoption. This is really, really impressive. So last year back when we initially announced Mweb's support within CakeWallet and we had a beta come out, there was less than around 40,000 LTC within the Mweb balance sheet totally. And then we announced Mweb and it spiked up a bit. But since then, it's been around a year, not even a year, actually, and there's almost 150,000 LTC on the mWeb balance sheet, which is huge. That's massive. That's a huge difference from last year. That just goes to show that people are actually using mWeb. They're actually sending a lot of their transparent Litecoin into the mWeb network. And I have to think that CakeWallet had a big impact on that and that's really cool to see that people are actually taking advantage of this feature now and seeing this adoption this massive adoption in volume and then Seth for privacy talked about this a little more in depth I was just going to mention it briefly we did add m-web support natively to cake pay so now you can pay for gift cards within CAKE pay natively using MWeb instead of just having to send to a transparent Litecoin address. That was all the slides I had, feel free to scan that QR code if you would like to try out CAKE wallet. It's very simple to use and easy to use and set up. We do have a booth at the exhibitor expo area over there. If you have any questions, feel free to come up to us. We would love to help you, love to answer any questions. It works on basically all platforms and the main ones that we support is, of course, iOS and Android, the mobile apps. Thanks, guys.
